HEIC and HEIF pictures: libheif, vendored as built
==================================================

libheif-bundle.mjs   libheif-js 1.23.5 (https://github.com/catdad-experiments/libheif-js), dist libheif-wasm/libheif-bundle.mjs, unchanged.
                     It is libheif (https://github.com/strukturag/libheif) and the HEVC decoder libde265
                     (https://github.com/strukturag/libde265), compiled to WebAssembly with Emscripten, the WebAssembly inlined.
                     Licence: GNU Lesser General Public License 3.0 (LICENSE-LGPL-3.0.txt; libheif's own notes in LICENSES-libheif.txt).
heic-worker.mjs      File Studio's own (MIT). It is the only code that calls libheif: it loads libheif-bundle.mjs as a separate module in a
                     Worker, hands it the bytes of a file and takes back the pixels.

To use another build of libheif, replace libheif-bundle.mjs with one that has the same default export (libheif-js's
libheif-wasm/libheif-bundle.mjs of another version does). The source of the libraries is at the links above; the exact versions are libheif-js
1.23.5's, which names the libheif and libde265 it was built from in its scripts/install.js.

HEVC, the video codec inside HEIC files, is covered by patents in some countries, and decoding it in software can need a licence from the
patent holders for some uses. The pictures are only ever decoded on the computer of the person who opens them, and only when the browser's
own decoder (Safari has one) cannot. Whoever distributes File Studio should take their own advice on this.
